tasks.name: P0.1: Last-visible-tab guard in close_page
tasks.desc: Add guard in `close_page` (navigation.ts) that rejects closing the last visible tab in the last visible window. Applies to ALL modes (sidepanel, newtab, MCP). Check: list visible pages → if closing this one leaves 0 visible → reject.

comments.author: investigation
comments.body: Root cause of browser self-closing. Chromium's CloseTab has no last-tab protection. Verified down to browser_handler.cc:CloseTab() → tab_strip->CloseWebContentsAt() with no guard.

comments.author: claude-verification
comments.body: Confirmed: sidepanel mode has NO guard at all. Only newtab checks origin === 'newtab'. MCP callers have ctx.session = undefined so even newtab guard is bypassed.

checks: close_page rejects when target is last visible tab in last visible window
Hidden tabs do NOT count as visible
Scheduled tasks (hidden pages) are not blocked
Works for sidepanel, newtab, AND MCP modes
Error message is clear: 'Cannot close the last visible tab'
tasks.notes: I20 ceremony: 118 task-specific tests pass (0 fail). 1847 total suite pass. All 14 tasks verified complete. READY FOR MERGE.

tasks.name: P0.2: Last-visible-window guard in close_window
tasks.desc: Add guard in `close_window` (windows.ts) that rejects closing the last visible window. No guard exists currently in ANY mode. close_window calls CDP Browser.closeWindow → Chromium closes immediately.

comments.author: investigation
comments.body: close_window has ZERO protection — not even in newtab mode. Verified: windows.ts handler directly calls ctx.browser.closeWindow(args.windowId) with no checks.

comments.author: claude-verification
comments.body: Also check set_window_visibility — deny hiding the last visible window (indirect bypass: hide all windows → close hidden).

checks: close_window rejects when target is last visible window
Hidden windows do NOT count as visible
set_window_visibility rejects hiding the last visible window
Error message is clear: 'Cannot close the last visible window'
tasks.notes: Last-visible-window guard in close_window + set_window_visibility. 10 unit tests passing (I20: added data: URL edge-case).

tasks.name: P0.3: Sidepanel origin-tab guard for close_page and navigate_page
tasks.desc: Extend the existing newtab-only guard to also protect the sidepanel active tab. In sidepanel mode, the active tab from browserContext is the origin tab — closing/navigating it disrupts the user's workflow. Add sidepanel to the origin check.

comments.author: investigation
comments.body: Current guard: `ctx.session?.origin === 'newtab'` — sidepanel mode is completely unprotected. The LLM can close/navigate the tab the user is viewing while chatting from the sidepanel.

comments.author: claude-verification
comments.body: navigate_page guard should be narrowed to action === 'url' only. Back/forward/reload on the origin tab is safe (doesn't destroy the chat UI). Current guard over-blocks these in newtab mode (V7).

checks: close_page rejects when target is the sidepanel origin tab
navigate_page rejects URL navigation on sidepanel origin tab
navigate_page ALLOWS back/forward/reload on origin tab (both modes)
new_page still works (creates background tabs)
Does NOT break scheduled tasks (they use hidden pages)
tasks.notes: Extended origin-tab guard to sidepanel mode. navigate_page guard narrowed to URL action only (back/forward/reload safe). 11 unit tests passing.

tasks.name: P0.4: close_tab_group guard
tasks.desc: Add guard in `close_tab_group` (tab-groups.ts) — currently zero protection. If a tab group contains the last visible tab(s), closing it would close the browser. Check before closing.

comments.author: claude-verification
comments.body: NEW finding: close_tab_group bypasses close_page entirely — it calls CDP closeTabGroup which closes all tabs in the group at the Chromium level. Zero guards in tab-groups.ts.

checks: close_tab_group rejects if closing the group would leave 0 visible tabs
Works when group contains the last visible tab
Ungrouping tabs (ungroup_tabs) is NOT blocked — just removes group, doesn't close tabs
Hidden tabs in group do not count toward visible count
tasks.notes: close_tab_group guard checks if group contains last visible tabs. 6 unit tests passing.

tasks.name: P0.5: Fix MCP session context (ctx.session undefined)
tasks.desc: MCP callers bypass ALL guards because ctx.session is undefined. The MCP route (mcp.ts) creates per-request servers without passing ToolSessionContext. Fix: derive session context from MCP headers and pass it through to tool handlers.

comments.author: claude-verification
comments.body: CRITICAL: MCP route has X-BrowserOS-Agent-Id and X-BrowserOS-Default-Window-Id headers but does NOT construct a ToolSessionContext. register-mcp.ts creates tool context without session field. ALL existing guards check ctx.session?.origin which is always undefined for MCP.

checks: MCP tool calls receive a valid ToolSessionContext
Origin defaults to 'sidepanel' for MCP callers (safe default)
originPageId is resolved from X-BrowserOS-Default-Window-Id header
All existing guards work correctly for MCP callers after fix
Per-request server still has no shared state (no regression)
tasks.notes: MCP callers now receive session: { origin: "sidepanel", conversationId: "mcp-${UUID}" }. All guards work for MCP. 2+2 tests passing.

tasks.name: P1.1: TabOwnershipRegistry in Browser class
tasks.desc: Add a TabOwnershipRegistry to the Browser class (browser.ts). Tracks which conversation/agent owns which page. Methods: claim(), release(), isLocked(), getOwner(), releaseIdle(), refreshActivity(). This is the foundation for P1.2-P1.4 and P2.

comments.author: investigation
comments.body: Zero concept of tab ownership exists anywhere. PageInfo has no controlledBy field. Browser class tracks pages by ID but no ownership. Multiple conversations can (and do) operate on same tabs simultaneously.

comments.author: design
comments.body: Registry must live on Browser class (singleton) not per-request — MCP creates per-request servers. Shared state must be at the Browser level.

checks: claim() prevents double-claiming by different conversations
release() only works for the owning conversation
releaseIdle() correctly sweeps stale locks
refreshActivity() touches lastActivityAt
Thread-safe for concurrent MCP requests
No regression on existing Browser API
tasks.notes: TabOwnershipRegistry with 37 unit tests. TOCTOU race + idle sweep callback + lifecycle tests added I22.

tasks.name: P1.2: Enforce tab ownership in tool handlers
tasks.desc: Wire TabOwnershipRegistry into tool handlers (close_page, navigate_page, click, fill, type, evaluate). When a tool targets a page, check if it's owned by another conversation. If strict mode: reject. If non-strict: warn but proceed. Auto-claim on first tool use per page per conversation.

comments.author: design
comments.body: Opt-in via config: tab_ownership_strict (default: false). When false, log warning but don't block. When true, reject tool calls on locked tabs. This avoids breaking existing workflows during rollout.

checks: Tool handlers check ownership before executing on a page
Auto-claim on first tool use per page per conversation
Strict mode rejects; non-strict mode warns
Ownership released when conversation ends
No regression on single-conversation usage
tasks.notes: Centralized ownership enforcement in executeTool(). Now checks both args.page (scalar) and args.pageIds (array). conversationId wired for chat+MCP paths. 8 tests. Fixed unnecessary cast in enforceOwnership.

tasks.name: P1.3: Enrich list_pages with ownership info
tasks.desc: Extend list_pages response to include `controlledBy: { conversationId, agentId } | null` per page. LLM sessions need this to know which tabs are already taken before attempting to interact.

comments.author: user-intent
comments.body: User asked: 'how to LLM in 1 tab know that the other tabs is currently control it?' — list_pages enrichment directly addresses this. LLM calls list_pages → sees controlledBy → knows which tabs are taken.

checks: list_pages response includes controlledBy field per page
controlledBy is null for unlocked pages
controlledBy shows conversationId and agentId for locked pages
MCP callers also see ownership info
PageInfo type updated
tasks.notes: Added controlledBy field to list_pages response with ownership info. 6 unit tests passing.

tasks.name: P1.4: MCP tab ownership tools (lock_tab / unlock_tab)
tasks.desc: Add explicit MCP tools for tab locking: lock_tab(page) claims ownership, unlock_tab(page) releases it. Lets MCP callers manage ownership explicitly rather than relying on auto-claim.

comments.author: user-intent
comments.body: User asked: 'have the option that make LLM to not allowed to interact with controlled tabs' and 'which from mcp' — explicit lock/unlock tools let MCP callers declare intent.

checks: lock_tool claims ownership for the calling conversation
unlock_tool releases ownership
Cannot lock a page already owned by another conversation
Tools appear in MCP tool list
list_pages reflects lock state
tasks.notes: Added lock_tab and unlock_tab tools. Registered in tool registry. Added agentId to ToolSessionContext. 11 unit tests passing.

tasks.name: P2.1: Extend glow.content with ownership indicator
tasks.desc: Extend the existing glow.content content script to show a persistent ownership indicator (badge/chip) on controlled tabs. Enrich GlowMessage type with { agentName, lockHeld, controlledBy }. Keep existing pulsing border behavior.

comments.author: user-intent
comments.body: User asked: 'can we implement it as another plugins itself ? or inside the current plugins itself ?' — Answer: extend existing glow.content. Already has the content script + messaging infrastructure.

comments.author: investigation
comments.body: glow.content already runs on all pages (*://*/*), injects pulsing orange border, has stop button. useNotifyActiveTab.tsx already dispatches glow messages with conversationId + isActive. Just need to enrich the message and add persistent indicator.

checks: GlowMessage type includes agentName, lockHeld, controlledBy
Persistent badge/chip shows on controlled tabs
Existing pulsing border behavior preserved
Stop button still works
Badge updates when ownership changes
Badge disappears when ownership released
tasks.notes: Extended GlowMessage with ownership fields. Added persistent badge rendering in content script. Existing glow behavior preserved. 5 type contract tests.

tasks.name: P2.2: Wire TabOwnershipRegistry to glow dispatch
tasks.desc: Wire TabOwnershipRegistry changes to emit events that the sidepanel's useNotifyActiveTab listens to. Enrich GlowMessage with ownership data from the registry. MCP callers should also trigger glow.

comments.author: design
comments.body: Server → extension messaging path: Browser class emits ownership events → server sends to extension via existing messaging → useNotifyActiveTab enriches GlowMessage → content script renders indicator.

checks: Ownership changes trigger glow message dispatch
useNotifyActiveTab receives ownership data
GlowMessage enriched with registry data
MCP callers trigger glow via server messaging
No duplicate glow activations
tasks.notes: Wired ownership data from TabOwnershipRegistry to glow dispatch via tool output metadata. executeTool() enriches metadata with lockHeld + controlledBy. useNotifyActiveTab extracts and passes to GlowMessage. I8: added 7 metadata enrichment tests covering auto-claim, owned, unowned, no-session, stale-state scenarios.

tasks.name: P4.1: Idle lock release with configurable timeout
tasks.desc: Add configurable idle-based auto-release for tab locks. Config key: tab_lock_idle_timeout_ms (default: 3600000 = 1 hour). Periodic sweep (60s) releases locks idle beyond threshold. Tool calls refresh lastActivityAt.

comments.author: user-intent
comments.body: User asked: 'it can have configuration to release that lock after some idle time (like 1 hour)' — direct implementation of this request.

checks: Default timeout is 1 hour (3600000ms)
Sweep runs every 60s
Tool calls refresh lastActivityAt
Configurable via server config
Release fires event for glow cleanup
No lock leaks on conversation end
tasks.notes: Idle lock release with configurable timeout. startIdleSweep/stopIdleSweep on TabOwnershipRegistry. onLockReleased callback for glow cleanup. Config keys in shared constants. Browser starts sweep in constructor. 19 unit tests. I6: fixed timing race in idle sweep test.

tasks.name: P4.2: Strict mode configuration toggle
tasks.desc: Add config key tab_ownership_strict (default: false). When true: reject tool calls on locked tabs. When false: warn but allow. Allows gradual rollout without breaking existing workflows.

comments.author: design
comments.body: Non-strict default ensures no breaking changes during rollout. Users can opt into strict mode after verifying their workflows.

checks: Default is non-strict (warn only)
Strict mode rejects with clear error showing lock owner
Configurable per-conversation or global
Warning includes conversationId of lock owner
tasks.notes: Strict mode config toggle. tabOwnershipStrict wired through ChatRouteDeps -> MCP route -> McpServiceDeps -> ToolContext. Default false. 9 tests.

tasks.name: V6 Mitigation: Neutralize window.close() in evaluate_script
tasks.desc: evaluate_script can run window.close() which bypasses all tool-level guards. Inject Object.defineProperty override on controlled pages to neutralize window.close(). Low priority — requires page-level injection.

comments.author: claude-verification
comments.body: Could-fix. LLM can inject window.close() via evaluate_script which bypasses close_page guard entirely. Defense in depth only — unlikely in normal usage.

checks: window.close() overridden on pages with active LLM sessions
Override logs warning instead of closing
Restore original window.close on session end
Does not break legitimate page close flows
tasks.notes: Neutralize window.close() in evaluate_script. wrapWithWindowCloseGuard() wraps expressions with preamble that overrides window.close with no-op. Original restored via try/finally. 10 unit tests.
